classification.difficultyReason: Choose an intermediate angle connecting the given and target angles, then switch between two marked parallel pairs to build the explicitly requested two-step argument.

content.prompt: Find the size of the marked angle $\angle AVB$ in each diagram below. The solution to each part will require at least two steps, each with its own reason.

spec.description: Quadrilateral WAVB with two distinct parallel-line families, given angle at W and marked interior angle at V. Decorative source blue is replaced by house black.
spec.mathematics: WB parallel AV; WA parallel BV; angle BWA = 43 degrees; find angle AVB. Drawing is schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 43-degree angle is visible.

answer.worked:
$\angle WAV=180^\circ-43^\circ=137^\circ$ (co-interior angles, $WB\parallel AV$).

$\angle AVB=180^\circ-137^\circ=43^\circ$ (co-interior angles, $AW\parallel BV$).

spec.description: Open zigzag AVBPQ with single and double parallel arrows, the supplied angle at P and the marked angle at V. Ordinary marks use black.
spec.mathematics: AV parallel BP; VB parallel PQ; angle BPQ = 85 degrees; find angle AVB. Drawing is schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: The 85-degree given remains visible; the requested angle is unlabelled.

answer.worked:
$\angle PBV=85^\circ$ (alternate angles, $PQ\parallel VB$).

$\angle AVB=85^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AV\parallel BP$).

spec.description: Circle with chords PQ, AQ and AV and horizontal tangent BVC at its lowest point V. Single arrows identify PQ and AV; double arrows identify AQ and BC. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: P, A, Q and V are concyclic; BC is tangent at V; PQ parallel AV; AQ parallel BC; angle PQA = 35 degrees; find angle AVB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 35-degree angle is labelled.

answer.worked:
$\angle QAV=35^\circ$ (alternate angles, $PQ\parallel AV$).

$\angle AVB=35^\circ$ (alternate angles, $AQ\parallel BC$).

spec.description: Hexagonal outline RBVATS with segment RA and all three distinct parallel-line families. No equal-side marks or regular-hexagon assumption. Ordinary marks use black.
spec.mathematics: BV parallel RA parallel ST; RB parallel TA; RS parallel VA; angle ARS = 45 degrees; find interior angle AVB.
spec.answerVisibility: The given 45 degrees is visible; the marked angle at V has no supplied answer.

answer.worked:
$\angle VAR=45^\circ$ (alternate angles, $RS\parallel VA$).

$\angle AVB=180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ$ (co-interior angles, $RA\parallel BV$).
